title: The Dark Moon Quiet Hour
skyStory: The moon has almost disappeared, three percent lit in Virgo, a whisper in the sky. It is taking a well-earned break, folding its silver laundry and putting it away neatly. The stars are brighter without it, showing off. Mercury hums a lullaby. Saturn turns down the volume of the universe by about twenty percent. Even Mars is being quiet, mostly.

reading: The dark moon is a reset button, and today it is gently asking you to press it. What is one thing you started this month that you want to keep? What is one thing you will let fade with this moon? Answer both before bed. Write them down.

Your energy will dip in the afternoon, and that is fine. The Fire Tiger needs dark nights as much as bright days. Take a quiet break, even fifteen minutes. Look out a window. Listen to the wind in the trees, which this week has a new, crisp, leaf-rattling sound. The [[The Hermit]] holds a lantern, but only when you need it.
joel.mission: Spend fifteen minutes today in total quiet, no phone, no music, just listening to whatever the world is doing.
joel.omen: A dark window reflecting a single light. A clear direction will show up once you stop searching.
joel.stoneWhy: dark stone for the dark moon

reading: The moon is nearly gone, and the shore is darker tonight than it has been all month. That is a gift for you. Your Life Path 11 does its best listening in the dark, and something has been trying to get your attention for a week now. Tonight you will hear it.

Let go of one small thing today: a grudge against a printer, a guilt about an unanswered message, a plan that no longer fits. The [[Death]] card in tarot is about endings that make room, and this one makes room for something better. You will feel lighter by dinner.
nancy.mission: Write one thing you are releasing on a slip of paper and drop it in the recycling with a ceremonial flourish.
nancy.omen: A star unusually bright on a moonless night. Your intuition is especially strong; trust the quiet nudge.

together.text: Share one thing you are keeping from September and one thing you are leaving behind. Keep it short. The dark moon is listening and will carry the leftovers off into the night, neatly folded, labelled, and never to be seen again.

game.intro: Dark moon, quiet hour. The crew has dimmed the studio lights. Choose your silence and guess the other's.
game.question: You get sixty perfectly silent minutes. Where do you spend them?
